findings.issue: The item.mine (claimant) visibility branch is NOT deactivation-gated. Adversarial live-PG probe (my own, beyond the coder's 8 AC): a DEACTIVATED actor who CLAIMED a task while active can still read that task's detail (GET /api/inbox/:id) with a residual-window JWT -> HTTP 200 (deactivation does not release the claim; claim-state -> item.mine=true is identity-match only). This is a real, but NARROW and NON-BLOCKING, defense-in-depth residual: (a) self-scoped -- only a task the actor personally claimed and already had full access to; (b) time-bounded to the ~300s residual JWT window (T-0702); (c) byte-symmetric with LIST's inTab("mine") (line 1184) and its 'mine' badge -- a deactivated claimant already sees the same task in LIST, so this is a SYSTEMIC property (deactivation != claim release; claim-state visibility is ACTOR_ACTIVE-gated NOWHERE), not introduced by T-0750; (d) the ADR (§3) honestly scopes the deactivation cutoff to branches (2) role and (3) owner ONLY -- it does NOT overclaim item.mine cuts off deactivated actors. The finding under fix (role-addressee / arbitrary-tenant-member read) IS closed (live AC-3 + my P4 both 404). Narrowing DETAIL alone would break the LIST/DETAIL 'mine' symmetry the task correctly preserves.
